item.title: A walk by the pond
item.description: Name plants, animals and things you see on a short walk. Use simple verbs to say what you do by the water.

children.definition: A small area of still water with land all around it.
children.example: Two ducks are on the pond.

children.definition: A bird with a wide, flat beak that often swims on water.
children.example: A duck swims past the bench.

children.definition: A small animal with long back legs that can jump and swim.
children.example: A frog sat on a stone by the water.

children.definition: One of the flat, usually green parts of a plant or tree.
children.example: A yellow leaf fell onto the bench.

children.definition: A low green plant that often covers the ground in a park.
children.example: You can sit on the grass here.

children.definition: A small, hard piece of rock.
children.example: Put the stone back beside the path.

children.definition: A long seat with space for more than one person.
children.example: Is there room on the bench for me?

children.definition: A narrow way that people can walk along.
children.example: This path goes around the pond.

children.definition: A plant with a thick, hard main stem and branches. Many grow very tall.
children.example: Meet me by the big tree at the end of the path.

children.definition: A long, hard part that grows out from the main stem of a tree or from one of its thicker parts.
children.example: There is a bird on that branch.

children.definition: To look at someone or something for a while to see what happens.
children.example: Let's watch the ducks for a minute.

children.definition: To rest with the lower part of your body on a seat or on the ground.
children.example: We can sit under the tree and eat our lunch.

children.definition: To quickly push yourself up into the air with your legs.
children.example: I can jump over that stone.
There is mud on my shoes after our walk.
